@graph.headline: 7 Gmail Alternatives for 2026
@graph.description: Compare seven Gmail alternatives for privacy, business email, custom domains and Apple or Microsoft workflows, with prices and migration limits checked on November 1, 2026.

mainEntity.name: What is the best Gmail alternative?

acceptedAnswer.text: Outlook.com is a broad alternative for Microsoft users, Proton Mail and Tuta Mail suit privacy-focused readers, Zoho Mail and Fastmail suit custom-domain needs, and iCloud Mail fits Apple users. The best choice depends on your storage, integrations, domain and migration needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I keep my Gmail address if I switch apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A mail app can connect to a Gmail account through a supported account type. This changes the interface, not the provider, storage limit or Google account policies.

mainEntity.name: Can I move old Gmail messages to another provider?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, yes, through the destination's supported importer or a Google Takeout archive. Check messages, attachments, sent mail, contacts, calendars and labels after import. Keep the original account until the new setup is verified.

mainEntity.name: Will Gmail stop supporting other email accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says web POP and Gmailify support for third-party accounts is being removed, with existing users supported until January 2027. The third-party Send as feature also ends in January 2027. Gmail itself is not closing.

mainEntity.name: Is there a free Gmail alternative?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Outlook.com, Proton Mail, Tuta Mail, iCloud Mail and Yahoo Mail have free entry points, but storage, account features and custom-domain support differ. Verify current limits in the official plan page for your region.
